provenance.instrument: O'Hara Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 455 Zoning, Ord. No. 1361 of 1-14-2020, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 OH0217, Township of O'Hara (Allegheny County named in 455-2.2 'Lot of record' and 'Allegheny County Department of Economic Development'). District use lists and lot, yard and height figures are text in Articles IV to X. The chapter has no attachments. Floodplain rules are in Chapter 230. New Laws: Ord. No. 1464, 1465 (Chapter 420) and 1466, none on zoning
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 Version Information: 'Includes legislation through 05-12-2026. Uploaded on: 08-22-2026.' New Laws: three, none amending Chapter 455
checks: 'Extended family living area' is a permitted accessory use in R-1, R-2, R-3 and R-4 (455-4.2B(14), 455-5.2B(13), 455-6.2B(13), 455-7.2B(13)). It is 'A separate living area in a home attached to the main home through a common door. The area may be used to house individuals related to the homeowner by marriage, blood or adoption. The space may not be rented out under any circumstances' (455-2.2). The code gives it no size cap, no count and no other standards. 'Uses of land, buildings or structures not clearly permitted in the various zoning districts are prohibited', and an accessory use with an 'ambiguity, indefiniteness or absence of standards' in the chapter 'shall not be permitted' (455-1.3). Read that way the listing is not clean, so the by-right reading is not settled

Whether the area may have its own kitchen is not settled. A dwelling unit has 'complete housekeeping facilities' and no enclosed space in common with another unit except vestibules, entrances, halls or porches, a dwelling is a building or part of one used 'exclusively for single-family residential occupancy', and a structure with two dwelling units is a two-family structure (455-2.2). Two-family structures are not listed in R-1, R-2 or R-4, and a duplex is a conditional use only in R-3 (455-6.3E)

A unit in a separate building is not allowed. The area must be 'in a home attached to the main home through a common door' (455-2.2), and a single-family dwelling may not share a lot with any other principal building (455-1.4). 'No accessory structure in the rear of a principal structure and on the same non-through lot shall be used in whole or in part as a dwelling' (455-15.19G) reaches only a building behind the house on a lot that is not a through lot, so the definition is the bar elsewhere

A structure joined to the house by a covered passageway or a common wall is part of the principal structure (455-15.19F). So an area made in or over an attached garage, joined to the house by a common door, is part of the house and may be an extended family living area. A detached garage may not hold one. An attached area meets the district yards. No structure may project into a minimum yard (455-15.1B)

Uses not clearly permitted are prohibited (455-1.3, 455-1.6), and 'Under no circumstances shall the Zoning Hearing Board grant a variance to allow a use not permissible under the terms of this chapter in the district involved' (455-20.7C)

CD-1 and CD-2 permit single-family detached dwellings but do not list the extended family living area (455-8.2). C and SM list no single-family dwelling. 455-1.5 bars residences there except by special exception, and neither district lists one (455-9.2, 455-9.3, 455-10.2). C allows mobile home parks by conditional use (455-9.3H)

Parking: 'Residential: two off-street parking spaces per dwelling unit' (455-16.1J(8)). If the area is not a dwelling unit, no added spaces are named. No driveway may serve more than two residences (455-16.2C(8)). An alteration that enlarges a structure by 20% or more must add the parking the alteration needs (455-16.1B)

Floodplain (Chapter 230): 'Within any identified floodplain area any new construction or substantial improvement shall be prohibited', unless a variance is obtained under Article VII (230-23). No new construction or development within 50 ft landward of the top of bank of any watercourse in an identified floodplain area (230-22D). The Zoning Hearing Board hears Chapter 230 variances (455-20.5G(1)(e))

Steep slopes: on 15% to 25% slopes no more than 75% of the area may be regraded or developed, on 25% to 40% no more than 30%, and none at 40% or more (455-19.3C). No more than 50% of a forest may be cleared (455-19.3D)

Nonconforming lot of record in separate ownership: a single-family dwelling and customary accessory buildings may be built though the lot is short of area or width, if the yards are met (455-18.2). A nonconforming structure may not be enlarged in a way that increases its nonconformity (455-18.4A)

Planned residential developments (Article XI) are permitted in R-2 (PRD-2, 20 acres) and R-3 (PRD-3, 10 acres). Their accessory uses are 'Customary residential accessory uses, such as garages, carports, private swimming pools, garden sheds' and do not name the extended family living area (455-11.3C(1)(i)). Buildings may be 3 stories or 35 ft, and each dwelling unit needs 2.5 parking spaces (455-11.5D(2), 455-11.5H(4)(a)). Lot averaging (Article XII) in R-1, R-2 and R-4 allows smaller lots in a subdivision of 5 acres or more (455-12.2). The Mixed-Use Overlay (Article XIV, Ord. No. 1447 of 11-11-2025) is a tract-scale conditional use for apartments, townhouses and mixed-use buildings at up to 20 units an acre (455-14.2B, 455-14.4A)

Riverfront Green Overlay: a riverfront infill development is a conditional use in the overlay and may include single-family houses, townhouses and apartments (455-13.2B, 455-13.7). It is mapped on the O'Hara Riverfront Overlay Map at the Township office. It is a development of its own, not a unit added to a house

Riparian buffer: a riparian buffer easement at least 35 ft from the top of the stream bank on each side is recorded with any subdivision or land development that holds a stream with a watershed over 10 acres, and no use or construction inconsistent with it is permitted in it (385-16). It reaches a lot only where such an easement is recorded
Nonconformities may not be grounds for adding structures or uses prohibited elsewhere in the district (455-18.1B). A nonconforming use may expand up to 25% by special exception (455-18.3E)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: O'Hara Township Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-16. Read: Articles I, III, IV to XIV, XV (455-15.1 to 455-15.45), XVI, XVIII, XIX, XX, XXI and XXII, 455-2.2, Chapter 230 in full, 385-16, the New Laws page and code searches. Not read: Article XVII (signs). 'Conversion apartment' is defined in 455-2.2 but no district lists it. Pass 30 (2026-11-26): the 455-1.3 bar gate is now adu.status_dispute, the status read two ways (a permitted accessory use under the district lists, or not permitted for its absence of standards under 455-1.3), with no code text changed.

term.note: Listed as an accessory use in R-1, R-2, R-3 and R-4. Not called an accessory dwelling. Searched for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, granny, caretaker, guest house, servant, living quarters, household employee, conversion and extended family

status.note: A permitted accessory use, for relatives of the homeowner only. No hearing named. 455-1.3 says an accessory use with an 'absence of standards' in the chapter shall not be permitted, and the code gives the area no standards beyond its definition, so the by-right reading is disputed

status_outside.note: CD-1 and CD-2 permit single-family detached dwellings but do not list it. C and SM list no single-family dwelling. 455-1.5 bars residences there except by special exception, and neither district lists one

status_by_form.note: The area must be in the home, joined to it through a common door (455-2.2), and a single-family dwelling may not share a lot with another principal building (455-1.4). These forms mean a detached garage or other separate building. A garage attached to the house is part of it (455-15.19F), so an area in or over an attached garage, joined by a common door, is the internal or attached form. 'No accessory structure in the rear of a principal structure and on the same non-through lot shall be used in whole or in part as a dwelling' (455-15.19G)

readings.note: 'Unless a proposed use can clearly comply with all of the conditions and standards provided in this chapter, or if there is any ambiguity, indefiniteness or absence of standards in this chapter pertaining to an accessory use, conditional use or a special exception, such use shall not be permitted.' The code gives the extended family living area no standards beyond its definition, and it does not say whether the area may have a kitchen. A use the chapter does not permit cannot get a use variance (455-20.7C)

status_dispute.note: Each district lists the extended family living area as a permitted accessory use, and its definition says what it is: a living area in the home, joined through a common door, for relatives of the homeowner, never rented

path.note: Listed among the permitted accessory uses. A zoning/building permit from the Zoning Officer

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of 455-20.7A. Dimensional only: a use variance is barred (455-20.7C)

use_variance_barred.quote: Under no circumstances shall the Zoning Hearing Board grant a variance to allow a use not permissible under the terms of this chapter in the district involved, or any use expressly, or by implication, prohibited by the terms of this chapter in said district

value.name: Duplex (R-3)
value.conditions: 'Duplex, triplex or quadraplex' by conditional use from Township Council. One point of ingress and one of egress. 5,000 sq ft of lot 'per dwelling unit for multiple-family uses', 50 ft wide, front and rear yards 20 ft, side yards 9 ft, building coverage 30%. 'In a residential district, for approval of a conditional use, the use must abut a regional street or a collector street, except where the applicant agrees to pave and widen existing roads as required by the Planning Commission' (455-15.24I). The approval lapses unless the use is substantially completed and occupied within two years (455-15.24K)
value.note: A two-unit building, not a unit added to a house. The lot is 5,000 sq ft for each of two units. A duplex is 'Two dwelling units ... one over the other or side by side, with a common fire wall' (455-2.2). New construction in an identified floodplain area is barred (230-23)

value.name: Riverfront infill development (Riverfront Green Overlay)
value.conditions: 'Riverfront Infill Developments ... shall be authorized by conditional use in the Riverfront Overlay' (455-13.2B). Residential uses may be single-family houses, townhouses, attached single-family houses, garden apartments and mid-rise apartments, with commercial uses (455-13.7A, B). The overlay is shown on the O'Hara Riverfront Overlay Map at the Township office
value.note: A development of its own on the riverfront, not a unit added to a house. Its lot and unit figures were not read

historic_bypass.note: No historic path for the area was found. 'Historic site or landmark' is defined in 455-2.2

districts_read_no_listing.note: CD-1 and CD-2 permit single-family detached dwellings without the extended family living area. C and SM list no single-family dwelling, and 455-1.5 bars residences there except by special exception, which neither district lists

value.condition: If the area has its own complete housekeeping facilities it may be read as a second dwelling unit, which would make the house a two-family structure. A dwelling is used 'exclusively for single-family residential occupancy'. Two-family structures are not listed in R-1, R-2 or R-4, and a duplex is a conditional use in R-3. The code does not say whether the area may have a kitchen.

'Within any identified floodplain area any new construction or substantial improvement shall be prohibited.' A new building is new construction. A variance under Chapter 230, Article VII may allow it.

'Within any identified floodplain area any new construction or substantial improvement shall be prohibited.' A variance under Chapter 230, Article VII may allow it, with the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation.

disputed_by.note: New construction is a structure started on or after September 9, 2014, with its later improvements. A substantial improvement costs 50% or more of the building's market value. So an addition to an older house that costs less is not barred. It may not raise the base flood elevation and must be elevated or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible

value.condition: New construction includes a structure started on or after September 9, 2014 'and includes any subsequent improvements to such structures', and new construction in an identified floodplain area is prohibited. So on a house started on or after that date any addition or improvement is barred unless a variance under Chapter 230, Article VII is granted.

A substantial improvement (work costing 50% or more of the building's market value) in an identified floodplain area is prohibited unless a variance is granted, and no improvement may raise the base flood elevation. Smaller work must be elevated or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible.

'Within any identified floodplain area, no new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse.' Development includes the renovation, expansion or alteration of a building (230-35), so this reaches work inside the house too.

disputed_by.note: For improvements to an existing structure in an AE area without a floodway, the 50 ft rule holds 'unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection regional office'

value.condition: Steep slopes: on 15% to 25% slopes no more than 75% of the area may be regraded or developed, on 25% to 40% no more than 30%, and no earth disturbance at 40% or more. No more than 50% of a forest may be cleared. No development, filling, piping or diverting of ponds, watercourses or wetlands.

In a planned residential development (PRD-2 in R-2, PRD-3 in R-3) the plan's own lots and yards replace the district figures. Buildings may be 3 stories or 35 ft, and each dwelling unit needs 2.5 off-street parking spaces. The PRD accessory uses do not name the extended family living area, so whether it reaches a PRD lot is not settled.

In an approved lot averaging subdivision (LA-1 in R-1, LA-2 in R-2, LA-4 in R-4) a lot may be 25,000 sq ft in R-1, 15,000 in R-2 and 20,000 in R-4, 115, 90 or 100 ft wide. Front yards 40, 30 or 35 ft. Side yards 20 ft each and 40 ft together. Rear yards 40 ft inside the subdivision and 60, 50 or 60 ft on its edge. Impervious cover 20%. All other provisions of the zoning ordinance still apply.

types_allowed.note: 'A separate living area in a home attached to the main home through a common door.' A structure joined by a common wall is part of the house (455-15.19F)

reading.value: If the area is a dwelling unit, 2 more spaces (4 in all). If it is part of the house, the house's 2 spaces only. An addition that enlarges the house by 20% or more must add the parking it needs (455-16.1B)
